<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Recoverability of Property and Equipment and Impairment of Other Intangible</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <b>Assets</b> <b>and Goodwill</b> &ndash; As of December 31, 2017, we had net property and equipment of $958.2 million, net other intangible assets of $298.4 million and goodwill of $46.2 million. As described in Note 2 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, we follow applicable authoritative guidance which specifies, among other things, nonamortization of goodwill and other intangible assets with indefinite useful lives and requires testing for possible impairment at least annually. We evaluate goodwill and other intangible assets for possible impairment annually in the second quarter, or when events or circumstances indicate possible impairment may have occurred. The methods, assumptions and business factors used in our annual impairment assessment, and factors associated with recoverability and other impairment considerations are described in Note 2 to the Consolidated Financial Statements and our &ldquo;Risk Factors&rdquo; above, and are not repeated here.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">M<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">anagement&#39;s latest annual assessment in the second quarter 2017 found the estimated fair value of each reporting unit and each indefinite-lived race date intangible asset substantially exceeded its associated carrying value except for NHMS and TMS race date agreements. As of December 31, 2017, the carrying values of non-amortizable race date event sanctioning and renewal agreements associated with NHMS and TMS were approximately $199.6 million and $98.8 million. The estimated excess of fair value of identified intangible assets associated with NHMS and TMS&nbsp;is relatively nominal at this time, heightening sensitivity to management&rsquo;s assumptions used in estimating future discounted cash flows and profitability and associated risk of failing impairment testing. The evaluation reflects, similar to challenges faced by many major sports, reduced visibility on profit recovery due to factors such as changing demographics, evolving entertainment choices for fans, appealing &ldquo;at-home viewing&rdquo; experiences and retirement of popular long-standing &ldquo;megastars&rdquo;. We have lowered our expectations for forecasted growth rates for certain revenues and profit recovery. However, those expectations and forecasts are based on many factors out of our control, and could be found unachievable. Such ultimate outcome could adversely impact our estimates of fair values, particularly for NHMS and TMS race date intangible assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In the past, w<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">e have realigned Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series (or other motorsports series) race dates among our multiple track facilities to potentially more profitable market venues. As further discussed above in &quot;Liquidity&quot; and Note 1 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, we obtained approval from NASCAR to realign one annual Monster Energy Cup Series and one annual Camping World Truck Series racing event&nbsp;from NHMS, and an annual Xfinity Series racing event&nbsp;from KyS,&nbsp;to LVMS beginning in 2018.&nbsp;Many factors and alternatives must be (and were) considered when moving races as further described in our &ldquo;Risk Factors&rdquo;, and are not repeated here. If future realignment or changes in our larger events, particularly Monster Energy Cup racing events, result in less than anticipated future profitability and cash flows, our speedway long-lived tangible and intangible assets could become impaired resulting in material impairment charges that adversely affect our future financial condition or results of operations. Management believes there have since been no events or circumstances which indicate possible impairment, and that no unrecognized impairment of property and equipment and goodwill and other intangible assets exists through or as of December 31, 2017. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Depreciable and Amortizable Lives for Property and Equipment and Intangible As<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">sets</font></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Depreciation of property and equipment is provided using the straight-line method over estimated useful lives of the respective assets. At December 31, 2017, we have net property and equipment of $958.2 million. We also have nonamortizable intangible assets of $298.4 million and goodwill of $46.2 million for race event sanctioning and renewal agreements that are considered to have indefinite useful lives because their renewal and cash flow generation are expected to continue indefinitely. See Notes 2, 4 and 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information on our property and equipment, other intangible assets and estimated useful lives. Useful lives are estimated based on outside cost segregation and valuation studies conducted on purchased or constructed speedway property and equipment and purchased intangible assets, historical experience, intended use, condition, available information for comparable assets, and other factors and assumptions existing at the time of evaluation. Management periodically reviews the estimated useful lives used to record depreciation expense, and believes such estimated useful lives are appropriate and no changes are expected as of December 31, 2017. Management also periodically reviews whether non-amortization of other intangible assets remains appropriate, and believes such non-amortization is appropriate and no changes are expected at this time. Because we have a material investment in depreciable property and equipment and intangible assets, changes in depreciable and amortizable lives, should they occur, could have a material impact on our future financial condition or results of operations.</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> </font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time, we repurpose various seating, suite and other areas at our speedways for modernizing our facilities, alternative marketing or development purposes such as offering expanded premium hospitality, RV camping and advertising areas, or wider seating and improved sight lines.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> Our accounting policies for recording associated accelerated depreciation and costs of removal and disposal are further described in Note 2 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, and are not repeated here. As further described in Notes 2 and 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, we repurposed or are repurposing seating and other areas at AMS, CMS, KyS, LVMS and NHMS, and recorded pre-tax accelerated depreciation of $11.1 million in 2017. Notwithstanding these and previous year non-cash charges, the carrying values for seating and luxury suites at each of our speedways are material. Depending on additional future management plans, we could record additional accelerated depreciation, write off remaining undepreciated net book value of associated assets, and recognize costs of demolition and disposal, all or some of which could have a material adverse impact on our future financial condition or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Realization of Receivables and Inventories</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Management assesses realization of accounts and notes receivable and inventories, including any need for allowances for doubtful accounts or inventories. Management considers such factors as, among other things, customer creditworthiness, historical collection and sales experience for receivables, and current inventory levels, current and future market demand, and trends and conditions for inventories. The assessment is subjective and based on conditions, trends and assumptions existing at the time of evaluation, which are subject to changes in market and economic conditions, including changes or deterioration in customer financial condition or merchandising distribution and other factors, that might adversely impact realization.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Income Taxes</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Our income taxes and deferred tax assets and liabilities are material to our current and future financial condition and results of operations. At December 31, 2017, net deferred tax liabilities totaled $201.8 million, after reduction for deferred tax assets of $11.1 million, and liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits totaled $11.7&nbsp;million. As of December 31, 2017, valuation allowances of $1.9 million are provided against deferred tax assets. Management has assessed deferred tax assets, after reduction for valuation allowances, and believes realization is more likely than not. Our effective income tax rates can widely vary from year to year for many reasons. On December 22, 2017, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act was enacted into United States tax law substantially amending the Internal Revenue Code. Effective January 1, 2018, the Tax Act permanently reduced US corporate federal tax rates from 35% to 21%, among several significant other changes and limitations. </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Our accounting and reporting for income taxes (including the Tax Act), associated assumptions, estimates, deferred tax asset assessments, and various other factors that impacted our tax provisions and rates for 2015 through 2017, and comparative effective tax rate information are further described in Notes 2 and 8 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, and are not repeated here. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Under current accounting guidance, we recogniz<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ed the effects of the changed tax rates and laws as of the enactment date, subject to Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 118 which provides for a provisional one-year measurement period for entities to finalize their accounting for certain income tax effects of the Tax Act.&nbsp;</font>In 2017, we recorded a provisional one-time material reduction of our net deferred income tax liabilities, and corresponding income tax benefit, of $119.4 million consisting of: (i) tax benefits of $120.2&nbsp;million using new lower federal tax rates under the December 2017 enacted Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and (ii) tax expense of $723,000 related to non-deductible executive compensation as we anticipate the performance-based exception on our cash compensation plans will no longer be applicable.&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We anticipate the Internal Revenue Service will be providing additional guidance on the accounting for non-deductible executive compensation. We plan to finalize the accounting for those provisional amounts upon filing of our federal income tax returns within our 2018 fourth quarter</font>&nbsp;or in earlier periods if additional guidance is issued<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">. At this time, we believe those provisional adjustments will not materially impact our future effective income tax rates, deferred tax liabilities or cash flows. Final amounts may differ from provisional amounts after further analysis, changes in interpretation and assumptions, or additional regulatory guidance that may be issued, among other things. See our &ldquo;Risk Factors&rdquo; and &ldquo;Liquidity&rdquo; section above for additional information on our income tax reporting, and possible impact of changes in estimates and assumptions on our future financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Legal Proceedings and Contingencies</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We are involved in various legal matters from time to time, and intend to continue defending existing or new legal actions in 2018. We use a combination of insurance and self-insurance to manage various risks associated with our speedways, other properties and motorsports events, and other business risks. See our &ldquo;Risk Factors&rdquo; for additional information on our liability insurance program and self-insurance retention. The likelihood of an adverse outcome and estimation of amounts are assessed using legal counsel on litigation matters, outside insurance administrators and consultants for insured and self-insured claims, along with historical trends, assumptions and other information available at the time of assessment. We accrue a liability for contingencies if the likelihood of an adverse outcome is probable and the amount is estimable. Legal and other costs associated with loss contingencies are expensed as incurred. Management believes amounts requiring accrual are properly reflected in the accompanying financial statements. Management does not believe the outcome of the lawsuits, incidents or other legal or business risk matters will have a material adverse effect on our future financial position, results of operations or cash flows. However, new or changes in pending or threatened legal action or claims against us, if significantly negative or unfavorable, could have a material adverse effect on the outcome of these matters and our future financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>RECENTLY ISSUED ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">See Note 2 to the Cons<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">olidated Financial Statements &ldquo;Recently Issued Accounting Standards&rdquo; for information on recently issued accounting pronouncements, their applicable adoption dates and possible effects, if any, on our financial statements and disclosures.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Interest Rate Risk</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Our financial instruments with interest rate risk exposure consist of cash and cash equivalents and our Credit Facility. As of December 31, 2017, there were $30.0 million in outstanding borrowings under our floating interest rate Credit Facility term loan. A change in interest rates of one percent on our floating rate debt at December 31, 2017 would cause an approximate change in annual interest expense of $300,000. Fair value estimates are based on relevant market information at a specific point in time, and changes in assumptions or market conditions could significantly affect estimates. There were no interest rate or other swaps at December 31, 2017 or 2016. As of December 31, 2017, we had availability for borrowing up to an additional $99.3 million, including $49.3 million in letters of credit, under the revolving Credit Facility as further described in Note 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Other Market Risk</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; As described in &ldquo;Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements&rdquo; above, we had aggregate outstanding standby letters of credit of $698,000 and $605,000, and no instruments or securities with equity price risk, as of December 31, 2017 and 2016.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:center;"><b><a id="report" name="report"></a>Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>To the</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b> </b></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>Board of Directors and Stockholders of Speedway Motorsports, Inc.</b></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have audited the accompanying <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated balance sheets of </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Speedway Motorsports, Inc. and its subsidiaries<b> </b>as of December 31, 2017 and </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">2016,<b> </b></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">and the </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">related consolidated statements of operations, of stockholders&rsquo; equity and of cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017, including the related notes (collectively referred to as the &ldquo;consolidated financial statements&rdquo;).<b> </b>We also have audited the Company&#39;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control - Integrated Framework</i> </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">(2013) </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In our opinion, the consolidated<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b> </b>financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2017 and </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">2016, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Also in our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control - Integrated Framework</i> </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">(2013) </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">issued by the COSO.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Basis for Opinions</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#39;s management is responsible for these <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, included in Management&rsquo;s Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appearing under Item 9A. Our responsibility is to express opinions on the Company&rsquo;s </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements and on the Company&#39;s internal control over financial reporting based on our</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&quot;PCAOB&quot;) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We conducted our<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud, and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our audits of the <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the </font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">consolidated<b> </b>financial statements. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Definition and Limitations <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">of Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">A company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (ii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (iii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&rsquo;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not pr<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">event or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">/s/ <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Charlotte, North Carolina</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">March 12, 2018</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have served as the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s auditor since 2007.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="financial" name="financial"></a>SPEEDWAY MOTORSPORTS, INC.</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="balancesheet" name="balancesheet"></a>CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEETS</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:right;text-indent:84.5%;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-td-statement-type="balance-sheet" data-td-taggable-table="" data-td-v2v-id="1520032174969" id="thunderdome-statement-805633">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" id="null" style="width: 100%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-indent: 0px;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: bottom;">
			<td style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; border-bottom: 1px solid rgb(0, 0, 0); width: 70%;">

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="notes" name="notes"></a>SPEEDWAY MOTORSPORTS, INC.</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>YEARS ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.2pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="8769" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1520032225357" id="thunderdome-statement-805637">

			<td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.3%;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:1.6pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27727485" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.</em></b></p>
			</td>
			<td style="vertical-align:top;width:97.7%;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:1.6pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Basis of Presentation</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash;&nbsp;The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Speedway Motorsports, Inc. and all of its wholly-owned and operating subsidiaries: Atlanta Motor Speedway LLC (AMS), Bristol Motor Speedway LLC (BMS), Charlotte Motor Speedway LLC (CMS), Kentucky Raceway LLC d/b/a Kentucky Speedway (KyS), Nevada Speedway LLC d/b/a Las Vegas Motor Speedway (LVMS), New Hampshire Motor Speedway, Inc. (NHMS), North Wilkesboro Speedway, Inc. (NWS), Speedway Sonoma LLC (Sonoma Raceway or SR), Texas Motor Speedway, Inc. (TMS), SMISC Holdings LLC d/b/a SMI Properties (SMI Properties or SMIP), US Legend Cars International, Inc. (Legend Cars), Oil-Chem Research Corporation (Oil-Chem), SMI Trackside LLC (SMI Trackside), Speedway Funding LLC, Speedway Properties Company LLC a/k/a Performance Racing Network (PRN), Speedway Media LLC a/k/a Racing Country USA (RCU), and TSI Management Company LLC d/b/a The Source International LLC (TSI) (collectively, the Company, SMI, we, our or us). Hereafter, references to &ldquo;the Company&rsquo;s&rdquo; or &ldquo;eight&rdquo; speedways exclude NWS, which presently has <em data-td-fact-id="27727486" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> significant operations and assets consist primarily of real estate which has <em data-td-fact-id="27727487" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> significant fair value. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Description of Business</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We are a promoter, marketer and sponsor of motorsports activities in the United States. We principally own and operate the following motorsports facilities: Atlanta Motor Speedway, Bristol Motor Speedway, Charlotte Motor Speedway, Kentucky Speedway, Las Vegas Motor Speedway, New Hampshire Motor Speedway, Sonoma Raceway, and Texas Motor Speedway. We also provide event and non-event souvenir merchandising and distribution services, and food, beverage and hospitality catering services under an outside management contract through our SMI Properties subsidiaries; provide radio programming, production and distribution through PRN and RCU; manufacture and distribute smaller-scale, modified racing cars and parts through Legend Cars, and sell an environmentally-friendly micro-lubricant&reg; through Oil-Chem.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">In early <em data-td-fact-id="27727488" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> the NASCAR<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> Sprint Cup Series became the Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series and that naming convention is used throughout this document.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Racing Events</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; As further described in Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727489" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2,</em> we derive a substantial portion of our total revenues from admissions, event related and NASCAR broadcasting revenue. In <em data-td-fact-id="27727490" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> we held <em data-td-fact-id="27727491" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">24</em> major annual racing events sanctioned by NASCAR, including <em data-td-fact-id="27727492" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em> Monster Energy Cup and <em data-td-fact-id="27727493" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Xfinity Series racing events. We also held <em data-td-fact-id="27727494" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> NASCAR Camping World Truck Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727495" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> NASCAR K&amp;N Pro Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727496" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">four</em> NASCAR Whelen Modified Tour, <em data-td-fact-id="27727497" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> IndyCar Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727498" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> major National Hot Rod Association, <em data-td-fact-id="27727499" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> Automobile Racing Club of America and <em data-td-fact-id="27727500" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> World of Outlaws racing events. In <em data-td-fact-id="27727501" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> we held <em data-td-fact-id="27727502" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">24</em> major annual racing events sanctioned by NASCAR, including <em data-td-fact-id="27727503" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em> Monster Energy Cup and <em data-td-fact-id="27727504" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Xfinity Series racing events. We also held <em data-td-fact-id="27727505" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> NASCAR Camping World Truck Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727506" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> NASCAR K&amp;N Pro Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727507" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">four</em> NASCAR Whelen Modified Tour, <em data-td-fact-id="27727508" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> IndyCar Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727509" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> major NHRA, <em data-td-fact-id="27727510" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> ARCA and <em data-td-fact-id="27727511" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> WOO racing events. In <em data-td-fact-id="27727512" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> we held <em data-td-fact-id="27727513" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">24</em> major annual racing events sanctioned by NASCAR, including <em data-td-fact-id="27727514" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em> Monster Energy Cup and <em data-td-fact-id="27727515" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> Xfinity Series racing events. We also held <em data-td-fact-id="27727516" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> NASCAR Camping World Truck Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727517" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> NASCAR K&amp;N Pro Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727518" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">four</em> NASCAR Whelen Modified Tour, <em data-td-fact-id="27727519" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> IndyCar Series, <em data-td-fact-id="27727520" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> major NHRA, <em data-td-fact-id="27727521" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> ARCA and <em data-td-fact-id="27727522" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> WOO events.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our <em data-td-fact-id="27727523" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727524" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> race seasons experienced an unusually high number of event weekends with significant poor weather. The more significant races affected by poor weather and other racing schedule changes during the last <em data-td-fact-id="27727530" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> years include:</font></p>

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:1.6pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27727553" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> poor weather resulted in delays in starting and completing <em data-td-fact-id="27727554" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> Monster Energy NASCAR Cup race held at AMS and BMS, and postponing and rescheduling <em data-td-fact-id="27727555" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> Monster Energy NASCAR Cup race held at CMS</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>The Battle at Bristol in <em data-td-fact-id="27727556" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&ndash;<b>&nbsp;</b></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27727557" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> BMS hosted <em data-td-fact-id="27727558" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> collegiate football games, <em data-td-fact-id="27727559" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> of which (the &ldquo;Battle at Bristol&rdquo; - including a large preceding concert) was substantially larger than the other due to team standings and public interest. Under the same accounting policy for our racing events, we deferred advance revenues and direct expenses pertaining to these events in &ldquo;deferred race event and other income, net&rdquo;, all of which were recognized when held in <em data-td-fact-id="27727560" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> These events had a material positive effect on our <em data-td-fact-id="27727561" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> operating results, and associated revenues and direct expenses are reflected in &ldquo;other operating revenue&rdquo; and &ldquo;other direct operating expense&rdquo;, and our &ldquo;all other&rdquo; reporting segment (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727562" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em>). Management believes reporting these results separate from our core business of motorsports operations is appropriate as we do <em data-td-fact-id="27727563" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have additional football games scheduled at this time (nor have any been held before). Those results are <em data-td-fact-id="27727564" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> indicative of future results that can be expected or forecast.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.7pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27727565" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> Monster Energy NASCAR Cup, Xfinity and Camping World Truck Series Race Date Realignments to Las Vegas Motor Speedway<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&ndash; </font></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">We obtained approval from NASCAR to realign <em data-td-fact-id="27727566" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> annual Monster Energy Cup Series and <em data-td-fact-id="27727567" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> annual Camping World Truck Series racing event&nbsp;from NHMS, and an annual Xfinity Series racing event&nbsp;from KyS,&nbsp;to LVMS beginning in <em data-td-fact-id="27727568" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em>&nbsp;We considered many factors, including the popularity, demand, alternative uses and revenues, and potential net increase in long-term future profitability from conducting additional annual NASCAR racing events in the LVMS market.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

			</td>

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:1.6pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b></p>
			</td>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Principles of Consolidation</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Revenue and Expense <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Classification</font></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We classify our revenues as admissions, event related revenue, NASCAR broadcasting revenue, and other operating revenue. &ldquo;Admissions&rdquo; includes ticket sales for all Company events. &ldquo;Event related revenue&rdquo; includes amounts received from sponsorships, luxury suite rentals, souvenir sales, commissions from food and beverage sales, advertising and other promotional revenues, hospitality revenues, track rentals, driving school revenues, camping and other non-admission access revenues, broadcasting rights other than NASCAR broadcasting revenue, and other event and speedway related revenues. &ldquo;NASCAR broadcasting revenue&rdquo; includes rights fees obtained for domestic television broadcasts of NASCAR-sanctioned events held at our speedways. &ldquo;Other operating revenue&rdquo; includes non-event merchandising revenues and Legend Cars and parts sales, The Speedway Club at CMS and The Speedway Club at TMS (together the &ldquo;Speedway Clubs&rdquo;) revenues, Oil-Chem revenues, TMS oil and gas mineral rights lease and related revenues, industrial park and office tower rentals, and revenues associated with the <em data-td-fact-id="27727570" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> &ldquo;Battle at Bristol&rdquo;.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We classify our expenses to include direct expense of events, NASCAR event management (formerly purse and sanction) fees, and other direct operating<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> expense, among other categories. &ldquo;Direct expense of events&rdquo; principally includes cost of souvenir sales, non-NASCAR race purses and sanctioning fees, property and event insurance, compensation of certain employees, advertising, sales and admission taxes, outside event support services, cost of driving school revenues, and event settlement payments to non-NASCAR sanctioning bodies. &ldquo;NASCAR event management fees&rdquo; includes payments to, and portions of broadcasting revenues retained by, NASCAR for associated events held at the Company&rsquo;s speedways. &ldquo;Other direct operating expense&rdquo; includes the cost of certain SMI Properties and subsidiaries, Legend Cars, Speedway Clubs, Oil-Chem, industrial park and office tower rental revenues, and expenses associated with the <em data-td-fact-id="27727571" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> &ldquo;Battle at Bristol&rdquo;.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Event Revenues and Deferred Event Income, Net</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We recognize admissions, NASCAR broadcasting and event related revenues when an event is held. Event souvenir merchandise sales and commissions from food and beverage sales are recognized at time of sale. Advance revenues and certain related direct expenses pertaining to specific events are deferred until the event is held. Deferred expenses can include race purses and sanction fees remitted to or retained by NASCAR or other sanctioning bodies and sales and admission taxes and credit card processing fees on advance revenues. Deferred race event income relates to scheduled events to be held in upcoming periods. If circumstances prevent a race from being held during the racing season: (i)&nbsp;generally advance revenue is refundable and (ii)&nbsp;all deferred direct event expenses would be immediately recognized except for race event management fees which would be refundable from NASCAR or other sanctioning bodies, and for sales and admission taxes which would be refundable from taxing authorities. Management believes this accounting policy results in appropriate matching of revenues and expenses associated with our racing events and helps ensure comparability and consistency between our financial statements. Advance revenues, and certain related direct expenses, if any, for track rentals, driving schools and similar activities are deferred and recognized when the activities take place. Management believes its revenue recognition policies follow applicable authoritative guidance. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Poor weather resulted in postponing and rescheduling<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;an IndyCar race at TMS from the <em data-td-fact-id="27727572" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter <em data-td-fact-id="27727573" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> to the <em data-td-fact-id="27727574" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> quarter <em data-td-fact-id="27727575" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> The Company offered to honor unused tickets through exchange for race tickets to TMS&rsquo;s Monster Energy NASCAR Cup race in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> April 2017 </em>or IndyCar race in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 2017. </em>The exchange offer expired in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 2017, </em>and cash refunds were <em data-td-fact-id="27727576" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> offered. Tickets exchanged for race events held in <em data-td-fact-id="27727577" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> were <em data-td-fact-id="27727578" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> significant. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2016, </em>we had deferred race event income of <em data-td-fact-id="27727579" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$524,000</em> for unredeemed tickets associated with TMS&rsquo;s <em data-td-fact-id="27727580" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> IndyCar race, all of which was recognized in <em data-td-fact-id="27727581" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>NASCAR Broadcasting Revenues and NASCAR Event Management (formerly </b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><b>p</b><b>urse and </b><b>s</b><b>anction) Fees</b> &ndash; NASCAR contracts directly with certain television networks on broadcasting rights for all NASCAR-sanctioned Monster Energy Cup, Xfinity and Camping World Truck Series racing events. We receive television broadcasting revenues under contractual sanction agreements for each NASCAR-sanctioned race. The Company periodically negotiates its sanction fees for individual races with NASCAR. SMI has separate <em data-td-fact-id="27727582" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em>-year Event Management Agreements with NASCAR under which our speedways will conduct Monster Energy NASCAR Cup, Xfinity and Camping World Truck Series and the All-Star Race events in <em data-td-fact-id="27727583" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and through <em data-td-fact-id="27727584" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2020,</em> and include annual increases in broadcast rights revenue and event management fees of <em data-td-fact-id="27727585" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27727586" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">four</em> percent annually. Under the agreements, NASCAR typically retains <em data-td-fact-id="27727587" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> of gross broadcasting revenues as a component of their sanction fees. NASCAR also retains <em data-td-fact-id="27727588" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25%</em> of gross broadcasting revenues for purses awarded to race participants for each race. The remainder represents additional annually negotiated event management fees paid to NASCAR by the Company for each race.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We historically presented the <em data-td-fact-id="27727589" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10%</em> portion of broadcast rights fees retained by NASCAR as both broadcasting revenues and related event management fees. We have now determined that such amounts should be presented net, and have revised the presentation of o<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ur previously issued financial statements. We concluded the effect on our previously reported interim and annual financial statements was <em data-td-fact-id="27727590" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> material. In addition, management believes the revised presentation provides consistency with that used by other companies that promote NASCAR racing events. We revised NASCAR broadcasting revenue and NASCAR event management fees by <em data-td-fact-id="27727591" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$22,423,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727592" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727593" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$21,747,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727594" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> The revision had <em data-td-fact-id="27727595" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> impact on our net income or loss, earnings or loss per share, balance sheet or cash flows. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">48</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Marketing Agreements</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We have various marketing agreements for sponsorships, on-site advertising, hospitality and other promotional activities. Sponsorships generally consist of event and official sponsorship agreements. These various marketing agreements can be event, speedway or period specific, or pertain to multiple events, speedways or years. Marketing agreements that are <em data-td-fact-id="27727596" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> event specific typically contain stated fiscal year periods. We receive payments based on contracted terms. Marketing customers and agreement terms change from time to time. We recognize contracted fee revenues, and associated expenses, as events or activities are conducted each year in accordance with the respective agreement terms. Our marketing agreements sometimes include multiple specified elements such as sponsorships, tickets, hospitality, suites or on-site advertising in varying combinations for <em data-td-fact-id="27727597" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> or more events or contract periods, although there is typically a predominant element. Contracted revenues are allocated between admissions and event related revenue financial statement categories based on the relative fair or retail value of the respective multiple elements as such events or activities are conducted each year in accordance with the respective agreement terms.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Certain marketing agreements contain elements of purchased property and equipment exchanged for multi-year marketing and<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> other promotional activities at <em data-td-fact-id="27727598" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> or more of our facilities. The associated assets and deferred revenue are initially recorded based on their estimated fair or retail values, with assets then depreciated over estimated useful lives and deferred revenue recognized into income on a straight-line basis as events are conducted each year in accordance with the respective agreement terms. Deferred revenues recognizable in each upcoming fiscal year are reflected as current liabilities in deferred race event and other income.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Long-Term Food and Beverage Management Contract</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Levy Premium Foodservice Limited Partnership, wholly-owned by Compass Group USA, Inc., has exclusive rights to provide on-site food, beverage and hospitality catering services for essentially all Company speedway events and operations under a long-term food and beverage management contract through <em data-td-fact-id="27727599" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2021.</em> The long-term agreement provides for, among other items, specified annual fixed and periodic gross revenue based commission payments to the Company over the contract period. Our commission-based net revenues associated with activities provided by Levy are recognized at time of sale, and reported in event related revenue and at times, to a lesser extent, other operating revenue depending on the venue.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Non-Event Souvenir Merchandise and Other Revenues</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We recognize revenue when products are shipped, title transfers to customers, right of return or cancellation provisions expire, sales prices are final and collection is probable. We use these same methods and timing of revenue recognition for products sold through e-commerce or our websites, which has <em data-td-fact-id="27727600" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been significant. Product sold on consignment with right of return or cancellation provisions has <em data-td-fact-id="27727601" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been significant.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Revenue Composit<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ion</font></b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Our revenues are comprised of the following (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Revenues described as &ldquo;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">other event related&rdquo; consist principally of commissions from food, beverage and souvenir sales, luxury suite rentals, advertising and other promotional revenues, hospitality revenues, track rentals, driving school revenues, camping and other non-admission access revenues, broadcasting rights other than NASCAR broadcasting revenue, and other event and speedway related revenues. &ldquo;Souvenir and other merchandise revenue&rdquo; consists of SMI Properties and SMI Trackside sales of owned souvenir merchandise during racing and non-racing events and in speedway gift shops (motorsports event related merchandise), certain SMI Properties sales of racing and other sports related souvenir merchandise and Legend Cars operations (non-event motorsports related merchandise), and Oil-Chem product sales (non-motorsports related merchandise). &ldquo;Other revenue&rdquo; consists principally of revenues from the Speedway Clubs, industrial park and office tower rentals, Legend Cars as the sanctioning body for Legend Cars circuit races, and TMS oil and gas mineral rights lease and related revenues, and also includes all revenues associated with the <em data-td-fact-id="27727602" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> &ldquo;Battle at Bristol&rdquo;.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Use of Estimates</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires extensive use of management estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at financial statement dates, and reported amounts of revenues and expenses. Actual future results could differ from those estimates. Such significant estimates include (i)&nbsp;recoverability of property and equipment, goodwill and other intangible assets, (ii)&nbsp;depreciable lives for property and equipment and amortization periods for intangible assets, (iii)&nbsp;accounting for income taxes, (iv)&nbsp;realization of receivables and inventories, (v)&nbsp;accruals for certain business taxes, uninsured business risks, litigation, and other contingencies, and (vi)&nbsp;deferred compensation obligations and accounting and disclosures of stock-based compensation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Noncurrent assets are<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> generally reported at cost except for cash surrender values of life insurance policies which are reported at fair value (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727614" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em>). Management evaluates these assets for recovery when events or circumstances indicate possible impairment <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have occurred. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>there have been <em data-td-fact-id="27727615" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> events or circumstances which might indicate possible recoverability concerns or impairment.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Land Held for Development</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> represents property adjacent to a regional outlet mall in the Charlotte metropolitan area which management plans to develop and market or possibly sell in suitable market conditions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Property and Equipment (Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727616" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em>)</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation is provided using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the respective assets. Leasehold improvements pertain primarily to industrial park, office and warehouse facilities, and are amortized using the straight-line method over the lesser of associated lease terms or estimated useful lives. Constructed assets, including construction in progress, include all direct costs and capitalized interest until placed into service. Expenditures for repairs and maintenance are charged to expense when incurred, unless useful asset lives are extended or assets improved. Associated cost and accumulated depreciation of fully depreciated repurposed or removed assets are eliminated.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time, we <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>decide to repurpose various seating, suites and other<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;areas at our speedways for modernizing our facilities, alternative marketing or development purposes such as offering expanded premium hospitality, RV camping and advertising areas, or wider seating and improved sight lines. When management decides to repurpose and remove grandstand seating and suites as part of managing facility capacity or other speedway facility assets, depreciation is accelerated and recorded prospectively over shortened estimated remaining useful lives of the assets, and accounted for as a change in estimate, beginning when management contracts and begins removal. Associated estimated costs of removal and disposal are also recorded at that time in &ldquo;other expense&rdquo;. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">When events or circumstances indicate possible impairment <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have occurred, the Company evaluates long-lived assets, includ<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ing tangible assets and intangible assets subject to amortization, for possible impairment based on expected future undiscounted operating cash flows attributable to such assets using applicable authoritative guidance. Assets are grouped at the lowest level for which identifiable cash flows are largely independent of other assets and liabilities when assessing impairment. Gains or losses on property and equipment disposals are recognized when disposed. Recording accelerated depreciation, gain or loss on disposal or impairment losses related to property and equipment is based on assessment of the associated facts and circumstances. Also, assets are classified as held for sale when management determines that sale is probable within <em data-td-fact-id="27727617" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In connection <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">with the development and completed construction of TMS in <em data-td-fact-id="27727618" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1997,</em> the Company entered into arrangements with the Fort Worth Sports Authority (FWSA), a non-profit corporate instrumentality of the City of Fort Worth, Texas, whereby the Company conveyed the speedway facility, excluding its on-site condominiums and office and entertainment complex, to the FWSA. The Company, which has the right to reacquire the facility, operates the speedway facility under a <em data-td-fact-id="27727619" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">30</em>-year arrangement with the FWSA. Because of the Company&rsquo;s responsibilities, including associated risks, rewards and obligations, under these arrangements, the speedway facility and related liabilities are included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>
