<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Other Intangible Assets</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <b>and</b> <b>Goodwill (Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727620" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5</em>)</b> represent the excess of business acquisition costs over the fair value of net assets acquired, and are all associated with our motorsports related activities and reporting units. Intangible assets consist predominately of goodwill and nonamortizable intangible assets for NASCAR race event sanctioning and renewal agreements (Event Management Agreements) and, to a lesser extent, goodwill associated with event related motorsports activities. Acquired intangible assets are valued using the direct value method. We have evaluated each of our intangible assets for these agreements and determined that each will extend into the foreseeable future. We have never been unable to renew these race date agreements for any subsequent year and <em data-td-fact-id="27727621" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> such agreement has ever been cancelled. Based on these and other factors, such race date agreements are expected to be awarded to the Company in perpetuity. As such, these nonamortizable intangible assets for race event sanctioning and renewal agreements are considered to have indefinite useful lives because their renewal and cash flow generation are expected to continue indefinitely. <em data-td-fact-id="27727622" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> direct costs for agreement renewal or extension have been incurred or capitalized. However, we are obligated to conduct events in the manner stipulated under the terms and conditions of the annual sanctioning agreements. We follow applicable authoritative guidance on accounting for goodwill and other intangible assets which specifies, among other things, nonamortization of goodwill and requires testing of intangible assets with indefinite useful lives for possible impairment at least annually.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Impairment Assessment Methodology.</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> We evaluate goodwill and other intangible assets for possible impairment annually in the <em data-td-fact-id="27727623" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter, or when events or circumstances indicate possible impairment <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have occurred. Management considers each speedway and motorsports and non-motorsports merchandising subsidiary a separate reporting unit principally because that is the lowest level for which discrete financial information is available to our managers and chief operating decision maker. <em data-td-fact-id="27727624" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> reporting units are aggregated, and <em data-td-fact-id="27727625" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> intangible assets are allocated or transferred between reporting units, for purposes of evaluating intangible assets for possible impairment. We evaluate intangible assets for possible impairment based predominately on management&rsquo;s best estimate of future discounted operating cash flows for all individual reporting units and identified intangible assets (using the fair value assessment provisions of applicable authoritative guidance). The inputs for measuring fair value are considered &quot;Level <em data-td-fact-id="27727626" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3&quot;</em> or unobservable inputs that are <em data-td-fact-id="27727627" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> corroborated by market data under applicable fair value authoritative guidance, as quoted market prices are <em data-td-fact-id="27727628" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> available. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Except for the <em data-td-fact-id="27727629" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> realignment described below, our annual impairment assessment did <em data-td-fact-id="27727630" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> consider the possibility that management <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>realign <em data-td-fact-id="27727631" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> or more other Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series racing events among its speedway facilities, whi<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ch could result in net higher or improved future projected cash flows.&nbsp;Such information was also compared to available market information for certain motorsports industry peers. Management considered recent market trading ranges of price to earnings and sales multiples, cash flow and other traditional valuation methods, control premiums, and other market information related to our common stock from historical and forward-looking perspectives. <em data-td-fact-id="27727632" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> weighting of evaluation results was believed necessary. Management also considered that the estimated aggregate market value for NASCAR race event sanction and renewal agreements comparable to our Monster Energy Cup, Xfinity and Camping World Truck Series races, combined with the estimated fair value for all other Company net assets, substantially exceeds its current market capitalization. Management believes the methods used to determine fair value and evaluate impairment were appropriate, relevant, and represent methods customarily available and used for such purposes and are the best available estimate of fair value. Impairment charges and associated operations are included in our &quot;motorsports event related&quot; reportable segment (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727633" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em>).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><em data-td-fact-id="27727634" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> Annual Impairment Assessment</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><i>, and Impairment of Goodwill</i>. Management&#39;s latest annual assessment was performed in the <em data-td-fact-id="27727635" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter <em data-td-fact-id="27727636" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em> The impairment evaluation considered NASCAR&rsquo;s approved realignment of <em data-td-fact-id="27727637" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> annual Monster Energy Cup Series and <em data-td-fact-id="27727638" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> annual Camping World Truck Series racing event&nbsp;from NHMS, and an annual Xfinity Series racing event&nbsp;from KyS,&nbsp;to LVMS beginning in <em data-td-fact-id="27727639" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> and anticipated associated net increases in our future long-term cash flows and operating profits. Among other factors, the latest assessment assumes projected cash flow and profitability recovery, using modest annual inflationary growth rates for projected revenue streams and operating costs (other than NASCAR broadcasting revenues and event management fees), and strategic amounts of planned capital expenditures. Management projected annual increases in contracted NASCAR broadcasting rights revenues, and associated NASCAR event management fees, based on historical and anticipated rates which are supported by recently negotiated multi-year contracts. NASCAR event management fees for years after <em data-td-fact-id="27727640" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2020</em> have <em data-td-fact-id="27727641" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been negotiated, and future annual fees could differ substantially from those assumed in management&rsquo;s impairment assessment. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our <em data-td-fact-id="27727642" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> annual assessment found the estimated fair value of each reporting unit and each indefinite-lived race date intangible asset substantially exceeded its associated carrying value except for NHMS and TMS race date agreements and SMIP<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s reporting unit. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727643" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> the carrying values of non-amortizable race date event sanctioning and renewal agreements associated with NHMS and TMS were approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27727644" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$199.6</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27727645" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$98.8</em> million. We recognized an impairment for NHMS race date intangible assets in <em data-td-fact-id="27727646" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> reducing carrying values to estimated fair value at that time resulting in nominal excess fair value in future impairment assessments. The estimated excess of fair value of identified intangible assets associated with NHMS and TMS&nbsp;is relatively nominal at this time, heightening sensitivity to management&rsquo;s assumptions used in estimating future discounted cash flows and profitability and associated risk of failing impairment testing. Management&rsquo;s assumptions considered the following factors and conditions. NHMS was acquired in <em data-td-fact-id="27727647" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2008,</em> largely before the severe economic recession, which we believe has resulted in long-term operating challenges for many major sports.&nbsp;Our <em data-td-fact-id="27727648" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> (and <em data-td-fact-id="27727649" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>) evaluation reflects continuing lowered estimated future cash flows because the economic recovery has been slower and weaker than previous forecasts (although improving), and ongoing lower than anticipated revenues for various major racing events. The evaluation also reflects, similar to challenges faced by many major sports, reduced visibility on profit recovery due to factors such as changing demographics, evolving entertainment choices for fans, appealing &ldquo;at-home viewing&rdquo; experiences and retirement of popular long-standing &ldquo;megastars&rdquo;. We have lowered our expectations for forecasted growth rates for certain revenues and profit recovery. However, those expectations and forecasts are based on many factors out of our control, and could be found unachievable. Such ultimate outcome could adversely impact our estimates of fair values, particularly for NHMS and TMS race date intangible assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our <em data-td-fact-id="27727650" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> annual assessment indicated that the carrying value of goodwill associated with SMIP, which conducts event and non-event souvenir merchandising, exceeded its estimated fair value <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">because of potentially unfavorable merchandising business model developments. As such, a non-cash impairment charge of <em data-td-fact-id="27727651" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1,117,000,</em> before income tax benefits of <em data-td-fact-id="27727652" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$419,000,</em> was reflected in <em data-td-fact-id="27727653" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> to reduce associated goodwill to <em data-td-fact-id="27727654" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">There have since been <em data-td-fact-id="27727655" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> other events or circumstances that indicate possible impairment<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">, and management believes our operational and cash flow forecasts support our conclusions that <em data-td-fact-id="27727656" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> unrecognized impairment exists as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017. </em>Our future profitability or success associated with the NASCAR race realignments described above could significantly differ from management expectations and estimates, and are subject to numerous factors, conditions and assumptions, many of which are beyond our control. Different economic or industry conditions or assumptions, and changes in projected cash flows or profitability, if significantly negative or unfavorable, could have a material adverse effect on the impairment evaluation and our future financial condition or results of operations. The evaluations are subjective and based on conditions, trends and assumptions existing at the time of evaluation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><em data-td-fact-id="27727657" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> Impairment of Other Intangible Assets</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <i>and Goodwill.&nbsp;</i>In <em data-td-fact-id="27727658" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> we recorded sizable non-cash impairment charges to reduce the carrying value of non-amortizable race date event sanctioning and renewal agreements associated with NHMS, and goodwill associated with certain event souvenir merchandising activities, to their estimated fair values. The various factors considered in our <em data-td-fact-id="27727659" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> annual assessment resulted in lowering our expectations for forecasted growth rates for certain revenues and profit recovery. As such, a non-cash impairment charge of <em data-td-fact-id="27727660" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$96,530,000,</em> before income tax benefits of <em data-td-fact-id="27727661" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$34,569,000,</em> was reflected to reduce the race date intangible assets to estimated fair value. Our <em data-td-fact-id="27727662" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> annual assessment also indicated that goodwill associated with SMI Trackside, which conducts event souvenir merchandising at our and other <em data-td-fact-id="27727663" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party speedways, was impaired because of potentially unfavorable developments associated with NASCAR&rsquo;s announced industry changes to the trackside merchandising business model. As such, a non-cash impairment charge of <em data-td-fact-id="27727664" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2,338,000,</em> before income tax benefits of <em data-td-fact-id="27727665" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$885,000,</em> was reflected to reduce associated goodwill to an estimated fair value of <em data-td-fact-id="27727666" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Deferred Income, Net</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> (noncurrent) as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727667" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> consists of (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Preferred Seat License Fees, Net.</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> KyS and TMS offer Preferred Seat License (PSL) agreements whereby licensees are entitled to purchase annual season-ticket packages for sanctioned racing events under specified terms and conditions. Among other items, licensees are required to purchase all season ticket packages as offered each year. License agreements automatically terminate without refund should licensees <em data-td-fact-id="27727668" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> purchase any offered ticket and are transferable once each year subject to certain terms and conditions. Also, licensees are <em data-td-fact-id="27727669" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> entitled to refunds for postponement or cancellation of events due to weather or certain other conditions. Net PSL fees are deferred when received and amortized into income over the estimated useful life of those facilities or recognized upon license agreement termination.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Deferred Speedway Club Membership Income.</i><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> The CMS and TMS Speedway Clubs sell memberships that entitle members to certain dining, other club and racing event seating privileges, and require upfront fees and monthly assessments. Net membership revenues are deferred when billed and amortized into income over an estimated average membership term of <em data-td-fact-id="27727670" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">ten</em> years.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Advertising Expenses</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Event specific advertising costs are expensed when an associated event is held and included principally in direct expense of events. Non-event related advertising costs are expensed as incurred and included principally in other direct operating expense. Advertising expense amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727671" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$13,324,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727672" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727673" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$17,321,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727674" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> (includes &ldquo;the Battle at Bristol&rdquo;), and <em data-td-fact-id="27727675" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$16,660,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727676" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> There were <em data-td-fact-id="27727677" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> deferred direct-response advertising costs at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>or <em data-td-fact-id="27727678" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Operating Leases</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We have various operating leases principally for office and warehouse space and for equipment used in conducting racing events and other operations. These operating leases typically have initial terms of less than <em data-td-fact-id="27727679" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year or are cancelable with minimal notice, although certain operating equipment leases include multi-year terms. Rent expense for operating leases amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727680" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6,411,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727681" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727682" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$8,730,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727683" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727684" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6,233,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727685" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> Various office and warehouse facilities leased from an affiliate (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727686" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">9</em>) are cancelable with minimal notice; however, such lease arrangements will likely be renewed annually through specific contract periods. We lease various office, warehouse and industrial park space under operating leases to various entities largely involved in motorsports. These operating leases typically have initial terms of <em data-td-fact-id="27727687" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year or more and are noncancelable. Lease revenue for operating leases, excluding the TMS oil and gas mineral rights lease receipts discussed below, amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727688" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5,676,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727689" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727690" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5,625,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727691" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727692" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5,343,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727693" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We recorded gains from disposal of certain TMS property in <em data-td-fact-id="27727695" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and AMS property in <em data-td-fact-id="27727696" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> and losses on the <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">write-off of certain development costs in <em data-td-fact-id="27727697" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727698" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Income Taxes (Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727699" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">8</em>)</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities for the future income tax effect of temporary differences between financial and income tax bases of assets and liabilities. Income taxes are provided using the liability method whereby estimated deferred income taxes, and significant items giving rise to deferred tax assets and liabilities, reflect management&rsquo;s assessment of future taxes likely to be paid, including timing, probability of realization and other relevant factors. Our accounting for income taxes reflects management&rsquo;s assessment of future tax liabilities based on assumptions and estimates for timing, likelihood of realization, and tax laws existing at the time of evaluation. We assess the need for valuation allowances for deferred tax assets based on the sufficiency of estimated future taxable income and other relevant factors. We report interest expense and penalties related to income tax liabilities, when applicable, in income tax expense. Cash paid for income taxes excludes any previous overpayments the Company <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have elected to apply to income tax liabilities. The Company has <em data-td-fact-id="27727700" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> undistributed foreign earnings or cash or cash equivalents held outside of the US.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We follow applicable authoritative guidance on accounting for uncertainty in income taxes which, among other things, prescribes a recognition thresh<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">old and measurement attribute for financial statement recognition and measurement of tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return, and provides guidance on derecognition, classification, interest and penalties, and disclosures. Evaluation of a tax position includes determining whether it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27727701" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> a tax position will be sustained upon examination, including resolution of any related appeals or litigation processes, based on the technical merits of the position. In evaluating whether a tax position meets the more-likely-than-<em data-td-fact-id="27727702" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> recognition threshold, it is presumed the position will be examined by appropriate taxing authorities having full knowledge of all relevant information. A tax position that meets the more-likely-than-<em data-td-fact-id="27727703" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> recognition threshold is measured to determine the amount of benefit to be recognized in the financial statements. The tax position is measured at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than <em data-td-fact-id="27727704" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50</em> percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>TMS Mineral Rights Lease Receipts</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; TMS, in conjunction with the Fort Worth Sports Authority, has a natural gas mineral rights lease agreement and a joint exploration agreement which, among other things, provides the lessee various defined property access and right-of-ways, exclusive exploration and extraction rights, and non-interference by TMS as extraction infrastructure construction and operations commence. TMS is required to coordinate directly with the lessee on roadway and pipeline logistics to prevent interference of TMS or lessee activities, and monitor regulatory and other contract compliance. The long-term lease remains enforceable as long as drilling or extraction related activities continue or certain prices levels are met. Under the lease agreement, TMS recognized royalty revenue of <em data-td-fact-id="27727705" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1,916,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727706" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727707" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2,139,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727708" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727709" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4,265,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727710" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Such revenues can vary from associated volatility in natural gas price levels and common diminishing well production,<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> as well as other factors outside of TMS&rsquo;s control. At this time, while extraction activities continue, <em data-td-fact-id="27727711" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> new wells are being explored, and management is unable to determine ongoing volumes of production if any or for how long (including common diminishing well production over time), or if natural gas price levels will further decline or remain steady or adequate. The agreements stipulate that TMS distribute <em data-td-fact-id="27727712" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">25%</em> of production royalty revenues to the lessee, and obligate TMS to spend amounts equal to royalties received on TMS facility and road infrastructure improvements beginning in <em data-td-fact-id="27727713" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> up to specified cumulative amounts. However, at this time, management believes <em data-td-fact-id="27727714" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> revenues will <em data-td-fact-id="27727715" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> differ significantly from <em data-td-fact-id="27727716" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> and that our infrastructure spending will continue to exceed anticipated future royalties similar to <em data-td-fact-id="27727717" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em> As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727718" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> there was <em data-td-fact-id="27727719" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> deferred income associated with these agreements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:2.7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Taxes Collected from Customers</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We report sales, admission and other taxes collected from customers on both a gross and net basis in operations. Such taxes reported on a gross basis amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727720" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5,372,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727721" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727722" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$7,642,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727723" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727724" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6,024,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727725" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:2.7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We follow applicable authoritative guidance which requires that financial and non-financial assets and liabilities measured and reported on a fair value basis be classified, disclosed and categorized as further described below. Fair value estimates are based on relevant market information and single broker quoted market prices where available at a specific point in time, and changes in assumptions or market conditions could significantly affect estimates. The carrying values of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, certain other assets and accounts payable approximate fair value because of the short maturity of these financial instruments. Cash surrender values are carried at fair value based on binding broker quoted market prices. Notes receivable and bank revolving credit facility and term loan borrowings are variable interest rate financial instruments and, therefore, carrying values approximate fair value. The fixed rate senior notes payable are publicly traded and estimated fair values are based on single broker quoted market prices. Other long-term debt bears interest approximating market rates; therefore, carrying values approximate market value. There have been <em data-td-fact-id="27727726" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> changes or transfers between category levels or classes. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:2.7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Concentrations of Credit Risk</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, accounts and notes receivable, and cash surrender values. Concentration of credit risk with respect to cash and cash equivalents and cash surrender values is limited through placement with major high-credit qualified financial institutions and insurance carriers, respectively. However, amounts placed often significantly exceed available insured limits. Concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivable are limited due to the large numbers and wide variety of customers and customer industries and their broad geographical dispersion. Also, a significant portion of our accounts receivable typically pertain to advance revenues for specific events which are deferred until the event is held. As such, exposure to credit risk on such receivables that could adversely affect operating results is limited until recognition of the associated deferred race event income. We generally require sufficient collateral equal to or exceeding note amounts, or accept notes from high-credit quality entities or high net-worth individuals, limiting our exposure to credit risk. Amounts due from affiliates typically can be offset to the extent of amounts payable to affiliates, limiting our exposure to credit risk.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Loss and Other Contingencies and Financial Guarantees</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We accrue a liability for contingencies if the likelihood of an adverse outcome is probable and the amount is estimable. Legal and other costs associated with loss contingencies are expensed as incurred. We account for financial guarantees using applicable authoritative guidance which requires, among other things, that guarantors recognize a liability for the fair value of obligations undertaken by issuing a guarantee.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">CMS<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s property includes areas used as solid waste landfills for many years. Landfilling of general categories of municipal solid waste on the CMS property ceased in <em data-td-fact-id="27727732" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1992,</em> but CMS currently allows certain property to be used for land clearing and inert debris landfilling. Landfilling for construction and demolition debris has ceased on the CMS property. Management believes the Company&rsquo;s operations, including the landfills on its property, comply with all applicable federal, state and local environmental laws and regulations. Management is <em data-td-fact-id="27727733" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> aware of any situation related to landfill operations which would have a material adverse effect on our financial position, future results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Recently Issued Accounting Standards</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727734" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em>&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="27727735" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727736" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> &quot;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727737" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606</em>): Section A - Summary and Amendments That Create Revenue from Contracts with Customers and Other Assets and Deferred Costs - Contracts with Customers (Subtopic <em data-td-fact-id="27727738" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">340</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727739" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">40</em>)&quot; which enhances comparability and clarifies principles of revenue recognition arising from contracts with customers that supersedes most current revenue recognition guidance. The guidance includes the core principle that entities recognize revenue to depict transfers of promised goods or services to customers in amounts that reflect the consideration entities expect to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services, and expands required financial statement disclosures regarding revenue recognition. The FASB has issued several amendments to the new standard, including Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727740" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727741" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727742" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">08</em> &quot;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727743" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606</em>) - Principal versus Agent Considerations&quot; clarifying implementation guidance for those considerations in Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727744" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727745" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727746" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> and Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727747" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727748" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727749" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em> &quot;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="27727750" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606</em>) - Identifying Performance Obligations and Licensing&quot; amending the guidance in Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727751" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727752" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727753" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> related to those items. The FASB issued Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727754" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727755" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727756" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">14</em> approving deferral of Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727757" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727758" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727759" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> for <em data-td-fact-id="27727760" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year, with such guidance now effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>including interim periods within that reporting period. The guidance <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be applied retrospectively to each prior period presented or retrospectively with cumulative effects recognized as of the date of adoption.&nbsp;The Company has completed its evaluation of the potential impact that adoption <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have on its financial statements, including associated accounting policies, processes, and system requirements, and believes those now in place will enable timely and accurate reporting. The Company has completed analyzing its revenue streams and associated contracts using the <em data-td-fact-id="27727761" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em>-step model provided in the new revenue standard, and continues to gather information for required presentation and disclosures. The Company plans to adopt this new guidance as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>using the modified retrospective method of adoption.&nbsp;We believe adoption will <em data-td-fact-id="27727762" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> result in a significant initial cumulative adjustment or materially impact our future timing or classification of revenue recognition.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727763" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727764" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727765" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em> &quot;Inventory (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727766" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">330</em>): Simplifying the Measurement of Inventory&rdquo; which requires measuring inventory at the lower of cost and net realizable value based on estimated selling prices in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal and transportation (changed from the previous guidance of lower of cost or market). This update also clarified various other inventory measurement and disclosure requirements. The update does <em data-td-fact-id="27727767" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> apply to inventory measured using the LIFO or retail inventory methods. The guidance is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2016, </em>including interim periods within that reporting period, and applied prospectively. The Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s adoption of this guidance as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2017 </em>had <em data-td-fact-id="27727768" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> significant impact on its financial statements or disclosures.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727769" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727770" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727771" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> &ldquo;Leases (Subtopic <em data-td-fact-id="27727772" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842</em>)&rdquo; which replaces all current US GAAP guidance on this topic, and requires lessees to recognize assets and liabilities arising from leases as well as extensive quantitative and qualitative disclosures. Lessees will need to recognize on their balance sheets right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for the majority of their leases (other than leases meeting the definition of a short-term lease). Right-of-use assets will be measured at lease liability amounts, adjusted for lease prepayments, lease incentives received and lessee<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s initial direct costs. Lease liabilities will equal the present value of lease payments. Assets will be based on the liability, subject to adjustment, such as for initial direct costs. Operating leases <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>typically result in straight-line expense, while finance leases similar to front-loaded expense pattern. Classification will be based on criteria largely similar to those applied in current lease accounting. The guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning&nbsp;after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018, </em>and interim periods within those fiscal years. Early adoption is permitted. The guidance is required to be applied using the modified retrospective approach for all leases existing as of the effective date, requires application at the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented, and provides for certain practical expedients. The Company is currently evaluating the potential impact that adoption <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have on its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727773" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727774" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727775" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15</em> &ldquo;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727776" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">23</em>) - Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments&rdquo; which provides specific guidance on <em data-td-fact-id="27727777" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> cash flow classification issues. The guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>and interim periods within those fiscal years, and should be applied using a retrospective transition method to each period presented. Early adoption is permitted, and any amendments must be adopted in the same period. At this time, the Company believes adoption will have <em data-td-fact-id="27727778" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> significant impact on its financial statements, and plans to apply this guidance to future classifications when applicable.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727779" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727780" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727781" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">04</em> &ldquo;Intangibles <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&ndash; Goodwill and Other (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727782" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">350</em>): Simplifying the Test of Goodwill Impairment&rdquo; which simplifies how an entity is required to test goodwill for impairment by eliminating Step <em data-td-fact-id="27727783" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> (measuring goodwill impairment loss by comparing implied fair value of a reporting unit&rsquo;s goodwill to the carrying amount of that goodwill) from the impairment test. Under this update, entities should perform goodwill impairment testing by comparing the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount, and recognize an impairment charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the reporting unit&rsquo;s fair value. The same impairment assessment applies to all reporting units, and entities still have the option to perform qualitative assessment for a reporting unit to determine if quantitative impairment testing is necessary. This update modifies the concept of impairment from the condition that exists when the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds its implied fair value to the condition that exists when the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value. Entities will <em data-td-fact-id="27727784" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer determine goodwill impairment by calculating the implied fair value of goodwill by assigning the fair value of a reporting unit to all of its assets and liabilities as if that reporting unit had been acquired in a business combination. The Company is required to adopt this guidance for its annual or any interim goodwill impairment tests in fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019, </em>and should be applied on a prospective basis. Early adoption is permitted for interim or annual goodwill impairment tests performed on testing dates after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2017. </em>The Company early adopted this guidance for its annual impairment testing performed in the <em data-td-fact-id="27727785" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter <em data-td-fact-id="27727786" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 2017, </em>the SEC issued Staff Accounting Bulletin <em data-td-fact-id="27727787" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727788" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118</em> (SAB <em data-td-fact-id="27727789" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727790" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118</em>) which provides supplemental accounting and reporting guidance on the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act enacted into United States tax law on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 22, 2017. </em>SAB <em data-td-fact-id="27727791" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727792" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118</em> provides for a<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> provisional <em data-td-fact-id="27727793" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-year measurement period for entities to finalize their accounting for certain income tax effects of the Tax Act. Under SAB <em data-td-fact-id="27727794" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727795" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118,</em> the Tax Act&rsquo;s income tax effects for which: (i) the accounting is complete are reported in the Tax Act&rsquo;s enactment period, (ii) the accounting is incomplete are reported as provisional amounts based on reasonable estimates (to the extent determinable) subject to adjustment during a limited measurement period&nbsp;until completed, and (iii) are <em data-td-fact-id="27727796" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> reasonably estimable (<em data-td-fact-id="27727797" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> related provisional amounts are reported in the enactment period) and entities would continue to apply accounting based on tax law provisions in effect prior to Tax Act enactment until provisional amounts are reasonably estimable. SAB <em data-td-fact-id="27727798" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727799" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118</em> requires disclosure of the reasons for incomplete accounting, additional information or analysis needed, among other relevant information. We plan to finalize the accounting for our provisional amounts upon filing of our federal income tax returns within our <em data-td-fact-id="27727800" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727801" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> quarter or in earlier periods if additional guidance is issued. See Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727802" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">8</em> for the Company&rsquo;s accounting and reporting of the recognized effects of the Tax Act. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em data-td-fact-id="27727803" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727804" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27727805" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01</em> &ldquo;Leases (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727806" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842</em>): Land Easement Practical Expedient for Transition to Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27727807" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842&rdquo;</em> which <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">provides an optional transition practical expedient to <em data-td-fact-id="27727808" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> evaluate existing or expired land easements that were <em data-td-fact-id="27727809" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> previously accounted for as leases under current lease guidance. Entities that elect this practical expedient should evaluate new or modified land easements at the date of adoption, and which should be applied consistently to all existing or expired land easements <em data-td-fact-id="27727810" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> previously accounted for as leases. Entities that do <em data-td-fact-id="27727811" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> elect this practical expedient should evaluate all existing or expired land easements to assess whether they meet the definition of a lease. This Update affects entities with land easements that exist or expired before adoption, provided the entity does <em data-td-fact-id="27727812" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> account for those land easements as leases under current guidance. Once adopted, this Update should be applied prospectively to all new or modified land easements to determine whether any arrangements should be accounted for as a lease. Entities should continue to apply its current accounting policy for accounting for land easements that existed before adoption of this Update. The Company is currently evaluating the potential impact that adoption <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>have on its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Other Information</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <b>(Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727821" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>)</b> &ndash; Depreciation expense amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727822" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$64,817,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727823" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727824" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$54,344,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727825" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727826" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$61,933,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727827" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> From time to time, we <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>decide to repurpose various seating, suites and other&nbsp;areas at our speedways for modernizing our facilities, and alternative marketing or development purposes such as offering expanded premium hospitality, RV camping and advertising areas, or wider seating and improved sight lines.&nbsp;In <em data-td-fact-id="27727828" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> we recorded non-cash pre-tax accelerated depreciation aggregating <em data-td-fact-id="27727829" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$11,055,000</em> associated with removal of certain seating at AMS, CMS, KyS, LVMS and NHMS, and expansion of LVMS&rsquo;s dragway. We have repurposed, or are repurposing, various seating and other areas into unique fan zones and modern hospitality areas, some similar to high end &ldquo;taverns&rdquo; or &ldquo;pubs&rdquo; and sports bars, and close to restart areas at certain speedways. CMS now has an outdoor&nbsp;&ldquo;Sun Deck&rdquo; with solar panels as part of our &ldquo;green initiatives&quot;. We also are expanding and modernizing &ldquo;The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway&rdquo; into a distinctive, lighted &ldquo;four lane&rdquo; racing configuration. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">W<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">e recorded non-cash pre-tax accelerated depreciation aggregating <em data-td-fact-id="27727830" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$313,000</em> associated with removal of certain TMS assets in <em data-td-fact-id="27727831" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727832" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$9,111,000</em> associated with removal of certain seating at CMS and LVMS, retired leaderboard assets at certain speedways, and a decline in estimated fair value of certain real property in <em data-td-fact-id="27727833" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> Costs of removal are included in &ldquo;other expense, net&rdquo; (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727834" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>). These charges are included in our &quot;motorsports event related&quot; reporting segment (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="27727835" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em>).</font></p>

The carrying amounts for goodwill and other intangible assets include accumulated impairments of <em data-td-fact-id="27727842" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$149.7</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27727843" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$148.6</em> million at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727844" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> Amortization expense on other intangible assets amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727845" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727846" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27727847" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$11,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727848" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727849" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$17,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27727850" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> Estimated annual amortization expense for each of the next <em data-td-fact-id="27727851" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em> years is <em data-td-fact-id="27727852" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> significant.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:2.7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27727874" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727875" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> we repaid Term Loan borrowings of <em data-td-fact-id="27727876" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$36,000,000</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727877" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$54,000,000.</em> There were <em data-td-fact-id="27727878" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> borrowings under the Credit Facility during those periods. <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27727879" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> we borrowed <em data-td-fact-id="27727880" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$50,000,000</em> under the Term Loan (for partial funding of the <em data-td-fact-id="27727881" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> Senior Notes redemption as further described below), and repaid Term Loan borrowings of <em data-td-fact-id="27727882" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$80,000,000.</em> At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727883" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> outstanding letters of credit amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27727884" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$698,000</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727885" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$605,000.</em> As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>we&nbsp;had availability for borrowing up to an additional <em data-td-fact-id="27727886" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$99,302,000,</em> including up to an additional <em data-td-fact-id="27727887" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$49,302,000</em> in letters of credit, under the revolving Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Interest is based, at the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s option, upon the Eurodollar Rate plus <em data-td-fact-id="27727888" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.25%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27727889" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.00%</em> or a base rate defined as the higher of Bank of America&rsquo;s prime rate, the Federal Funds Rate plus <em data-td-fact-id="27727890" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.5%</em> or the Eurodollar Rate plus <em data-td-fact-id="27727891" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1%,</em> plus <em data-td-fact-id="27727892" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.25%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27727893" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.00%.</em> The Credit Facility also contains a commitment fee ranging from <em data-td-fact-id="27727894" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.25%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27727895" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.40%</em> of unused amounts available for borrowing. The interest rate margins on borrowings and the commitment fee are adjustable periodically based upon certain consolidated total leverage ratios. The Credit Facility contains a number of affirmative and negative financial covenants, including requirements that we maintain certain consolidated total leverage ratios and consolidated interest coverage ratios.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27727896" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We completed a private placement of new <em data-td-fact-id="27727897" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.125%</em> Senior Notes due <em data-td-fact-id="27727898" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> in aggregate principal amount of <em data-td-fact-id="27727899" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$200,000,000</em> in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2015 (</em>the <em data-td-fact-id="27727900" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes), and an exchange offer for substantially identical <em data-td-fact-id="27727901" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes registered under the Securities Act in the <em data-td-fact-id="27727902" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">second</em> quarter <em data-td-fact-id="27727903" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> The <em data-td-fact-id="27727904" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes were issued at par, and net proceeds after commissions and fees of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27727905" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$196,816,000</em> were used to fund a portion of the <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2015 </em>redemption of <em data-td-fact-id="27727906" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> Senior Notes as described below. The <em data-td-fact-id="27727907" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes mature in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2023 </em>and interest payments are due semi-annually on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="27727908" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="27727909" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.</em> The <em data-td-fact-id="27727910" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes rank equally in right of payment with all other Company existing and future unsubordinated debt, are senior in right of payment to any future subordinated debt and are effectively subordinated to all existing and future secured debt, including the Credit Facility. The Indenture governing the <em data-td-fact-id="27727911" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes permits dividend payments each year of up to approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27727912" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.80</em> per share of common stock, increasable subject to meeting certain financial covenants. </font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27727913" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> Early Redemption of <em data-td-fact-id="27727914" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> Senior Notes</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; We redeemed all outstanding <em data-td-fact-id="27727915" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6.75%</em> Senior Notes due in <em data-td-fact-id="27727916" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> in aggregate principal of <em data-td-fact-id="27727917" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$250,000,000</em> (the <em data-td-fact-id="27727918" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> Senior Notes) at <em data-td-fact-id="27727919" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">103.375%</em> of par plus accrued interest in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2015. </em>The <em data-td-fact-id="27727920" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> Senior Notes were scheduled to mature in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2019. </em>We used net proceeds of the <em data-td-fact-id="27727921" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes, <em data-td-fact-id="27727922" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$50,000,000</em> of delayed draw Term Loan borrowings under the Credit Facility and cash on hand to fund the redemption, including redemption premium and transaction costs. We recognized a <em data-td-fact-id="27727923" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> charge to earnings of <em data-td-fact-id="27727924" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$8,372,000,</em> before income taxes of <em data-td-fact-id="27727925" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3,106,000,</em> for associated redemption premium, unamortized net deferred loan costs and transaction costs of <em data-td-fact-id="27727926" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3,134,000,</em> net of issuance premium of <em data-td-fact-id="27727927" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3,200,000.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Other Notes Payable</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27727928" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> long-term debt includes a <em data-td-fact-id="27727929" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3%</em> interest bearing debt obligation of <em data-td-fact-id="27727930" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1,049,000</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27727931" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1,206,000</em> associated with the purchase of real property at BMS, payable in <em data-td-fact-id="27727932" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">eight</em> annual installments of <em data-td-fact-id="27727933" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$194,000</em> beginning <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Other General Terms and Conditions</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> &ndash; The Credit Facility and <em data-td-fact-id="27727934" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes contain specific requirements and restrictive financial covenants and limitations on capital expenditures, speedway or other acquisitions, dividends, repurchase or issuance of SMI securities, restricted payments, equity and debt security repurchases, limitations or prohibitions on incurring other indebtedness, liens or pledging assets to <em data-td-fact-id="27727935" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> parties, consolidation, mergers, transactions with affiliates, guarantees, asset sales, specific types of investments, distributions, disposition of property, entering into new lines of business, and contain redemption and change of control provisions and premiums. The Credit Facility and <em data-td-fact-id="27727936" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes Indenture also contain cross-default provisions. We were in compliance with all applicable financial covenants under these debt agreements as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Subsidiary Guarantees</b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"> <i>&ndash;</i> Amounts outstanding under the Credit Facility and <em data-td-fact-id="27727937" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes are guaranteed by all of SMI&rsquo;s material operative subsidiaries except for Oil-Chem and its subsidiaries (which are presently minor). These guarantees are full and unconditional and joint and several, with the <em data-td-fact-id="27727938" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023</em> Senior Notes on a senior unsecured basis. The parent company has <em data-td-fact-id="27727939" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> independent assets or operations. There are <em data-td-fact-id="27727940" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> restrictions on the subsidiaries&rsquo; ability to pay dividends or advance funds to the parent company.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Quarterly dividends were declared in each period and all declaration, record and payment dates were in the same fiscal periods.
